To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplement type and concentration affect growing heifer performance, and that DDGS is an excellent energy source in a high-forages diet.
supplementing growing heifers with DDGS in place of DRC improves performance and efficiency.
DDGS is a good source of energy for growing heifers and that the frequency of supplementation has no effect on performance of heifers fed a high-forage (hay) diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high-forage, low-cost, low-impact diet for growing beef heifers.
the effect of supplementing growing beef calves with different energy sources on performance and the energy value of the different energy sources.
the development of a feeding strategy to improve the performance of beef heifers fed high forage diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of DDGS at 1.0% of BW as a supplement in high-forage diets can be an alternative to corn-based supplements.
DDGS can be used as an effective energy source for growing calves fed a high-forage, low-concentrate diet.
the inclusion of DDGS at 0.8% BW daily improved performance of growing heifers compared to the inclusion of DRC at 0.2 or 0.8%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DDGS is an economical and efficient source of supplemental energy for growing calves.

supplementing growing heifers with a high-energy supplement (e.g., DDGS) at a rate of 0.8% BW/d is more effective at increasing performance than supplementing at 0.2% BW/d or feeding the high-energy supplement at a reduced frequency.
DDGS is more palatable than DRC and that DDGS can be fed at a lower rate than DRC to achieve equivalent performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supplementing heifers with 0.21 and 0.81 % of BW daily of DDGS, DRC, and DRC +CGM can improve performance.
supplement frequency and concentration are important factors to consider when developing a feeding program for heifers.
supplementing with DDGS is more effective in promoting gain than supplementing with DRC.
